name: Gyrodrillmatic Excavationators
summary: In Stormwind's Dwarven District, Shoni the Shilent readies tunneling machines for Dun Morogh. Short on parts, she sends you into Gnomeregan to salvage them from rogue automatons.

sections.title: A Fleet in Need of Guts
sections.body: In Stormwind's Dwarven District, Shoni the Shilent prepares gyrodrillmatic excavationators for Dun Morogh. Gnomish engineers there aid their displaced kin. The machines will carry people and supplies underground, but these massive rigs cannot work without the mechanical parts Shoni lacks.

sections.title: Salvage in the Fallen City
sections.body: Gnomeregan once supplied gnomish high technology. Its ruined halls and nearby tunnels still hold machines worth salvaging, though malfunctioning defense bots, mechanical sentries, and clockwork laborers roam unchecked. Shoni sends you into the fallen city for two dozen bundles of robo-mechanical guts, to bring back to human lands.

sections.title: A Monumental Undertaking
sections.body: Two dozen bundles of mechanical guts provide enough scrap to repair one excavationator. Shoni still has nearly four hundred machines to prepare, so mass transport underground remains a slow undertaking. Each working machine is a small step toward regaining ground lost in Gnomeregan's fall.

faq.answer: A gyrodrillmatic excavationator is a heavy gnomish tunneling rig, also called a mole machine, built to dig and carry people or supplies underground. Shoni the Shilent is preparing a fleet to serve Dun Morogh.
Shoni the Shilent is a gnomish engineer in Stormwind's Dwarven District. Outspoken and demanding, she is preparing hundreds of mechanical diggers.

faq.q: Why does Shoni need parts from Gnomeregan specifically?
faq.answer: Gnomeregan once supplied gnomish high technology, and its fallen halls hold haywire automatons, clockwork servitors, and defensive mechs. The city's manufacturing supply lines are severed, so these rogue machines offer compatible gnomish spare parts.

faq.q: Where are the Robo-Mechanical Guts found?
faq.answer: Robo-Mechanical Guts can be salvaged from mechanical sentries, clockwork constructs, and other hostile machines in Gnomeregan's ruined facility and upper tunnel approaches.

faq.q: Does fixing one machine finish Shoni's fleet?
faq.answer: No. Two dozen bundles of mechanical guts repair one drill. Shoni says she still has 398 excavationators left to go.

faq.q: Why is an excavation fleet being prepared for Dun Morogh?
faq.answer: Dun Morogh is the gnomes' ancestral home and the site of their fallen capital. Heavy tunneling rigs can help dig, clear debris, and support work in the snow-covered mountain reaches.

angles.text: As a gnome, each salvaged component brings Shoni's underground fleet closer to working order. From Stormwind, the dream of reclamation and industrial recovery lives on.
As an engineer, stripping precise clockwork innards from Gnomeregan's fallen servitors offers a practical lesson in gnomish design and heavy machinery repair.
As an Alliance member, helping gnomes prepare excavation machines in Stormwind strengthens ties between their human hosts and the exiled survivors working to reclaim their heritage.
